question: When thermosetting resins were gasified in molten alkali hydroxide, why did the CO2 found in the gas phase increase with temperature?
expect: premise false: CO and CO2 were not detected at any temperature (0, below the GC limit); the CO2 formed is thought to be captured by the molten hydroxide as carbonate (Tables 1-2; sec. 3.2.1)

[Document: Dissolution and gasification behavior of thermosetting resin in molten alkali hydroxide]

The CO2 found in the gas phase increased with temperature because most of the CO2 formed during the decomposition of thermosetting resins was captured by the molten alkali hydroxide as carbonate (inorganic carbon) according to reaction (3), and possible byproducts, such as dissolved organic species and solid carbonaceous residues, are reflected in the carbon distributions shown in Fig. 6–8.
